newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian PM sees constitutional change this month.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian PM sees constitutional change this month.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Thursday he expected parliament to amend the nation's constitution this month, allowing ratification of an association agreement with the European Union.

"It is my estimate we (Slovenia) will end the procedure of constitutional change in June," Drnovsek told reporters. "Our aspirations of full membership of the European Union depend upon how fast we are able to change the constitution."
The constitution has to be amended to allow foreigners to buy real estate in the former Yugoslav republic.

The government on Thursday tabled draft legislation to amend Slovenia's constitution. The Constitutional Court ruled that parliament could not ratify the association agreement with the EU without constitutional changes.
The EU association accord, signed in June last year, requires Slovenia to allow foreign nationals to buy land within four years of the agreement taking effect.
Drnovsek said his talks with opposition parties led him to believe the proposed constitutional changes would gain the necessary two-thirds majority in parliament.
Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats and their coalition partners -- the conservative People's Party and the pensioners' party Desus -- hold 49 out of 90 seats.

The prime minister said the amendment would also improve Slovenia's chances of joining the NATO military alliance in its first wave of expansion as it would show the country was ready to adopt to the standards of developed Western countries.

European Commission President Jacques Santer said in April that Slovenia's speedy ratification of the association agreement was a precondition for it to be among the first ex-communist states to start negotiations on EU membership, probably in 1998.
